title: public-surface-sweep-guard
universal_lens: A lattice of information-flow predicates over a file-system poset: each route/page is a node; keep-out patterns form a forbidden antichain; gate resolution is a monotone closure operator on the ancestor lattice; allow-list entries are distinguished elements that must not mask predicate failure. The guard computes the least fixed point of (pattern-match ∧ ¬gate-closure) and asserts emptiness.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats each keep-out pattern as a latent variable with a conformal non-exposure guarantee. The sweep constructs a prediction set over public surfaces: coverage = 1 − α where α is the false-negative rate measured by injected leaks. Ancestor-layout resolution implements a hierarchical Bayesian prior that gates propagate downward; allow-list masking is a prior-data conflict detected by leave-one-out cross-validation on regression cases.
gse_mapping: GSE models the CI pipeline as a state-transition system: states = {clean, leak-detected, guard-broken}; transitions triggered by pattern-match events and gate-resolution queries. The three injected leaks are adversarial probes that verify the transition function's soundness. Cron-helper authentication is a policy-compliance edge case where the guard's observation function must recognize indirect authorization via helper calls, not literal strings.

primitives.name: Keep-Out Pattern Sweep Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each file is matched against twelve keep-out patterns taken verbatim from the doctrine's keep-out list (raw NGS rows, QBR, separation, WOPR, EPA, signal ledger, calibration internals, edge internals, adjustment layer, truth-catalog topology, source registry, raw player-week rows).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F: set of 445 route/page files (dimensionless count); \mathcal{P}: set of 12 keep-out patterns (dimensionless); match(p,f): predicate → {0,1}; \mathcal{S}: findings set (dimensionless count)
primitives.assumptions: Patterns are literal substrings/regexes from doctrine; file corpus static during sweep; no dynamic code generation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pattern set \mathcal{P} incomplete (missing variants); match function case-sensitive (Bug 1); false positives from comments/JSDoc/marketing copy.

layer2.mapping: GSI: \mathcal{P} ≡ forbidden feature set; match ≡ conformal score exceedance. GSE: sweep ≡ safety monitor transition; findings ≡ alarm states.
layer2.telemetry: Findings count (42), false-positive rate (vocabulary hits), false-negative rate (injected leaks caught)

primitives.name: Ancestor-Layout Gate Closure Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: A match is a **finding** only if the surface is also ungated: no gate in the file, no gate in an ancestor layout, and no recorded allow-list entry.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: gate(x): predicate → {0,1} for file or layout; ancestors(f): poset of ancestor layouts; allowlist(f): predicate → {0,1}; gated(f): composite predicate → {0,1}
primitives.assumptions: Gate syntax recognized in both polarities (=== 'true' and !== 'true'); redirect structural check: handler cannot render at all; allow-list entries are explicit opt-outs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Gate polarity mismatch (Bug 2); partial redirect counted as gate (Bug 3); allow-list masking broken predicate (stats/* pages).

layer2.mapping: GSI: gated(·) ≡ posterior probability of exposure < threshold; ancestor propagation ≡ hierarchical shrinkage. GSE: gate resolution ≡ policy evaluation in state machine; allow-list ≡ exception state.
layer2.telemetry: Gate detection recall (polarity coverage), redirect structural analysis precision, allow-list masking detection (3 entries removed, suite green)

primitives.name: Leak-Injection Regression Verification Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each of the following was found by injecting a real leak and confirming the suite went red: 1.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: G: guard function; \ell_i: injected leak i (i=1..3); inject(·): mutation operator; \mathbb{1}: indicator; \mathcal{V}: verification predicate → {0,1}
primitives.assumptions: Injected leaks are representative of real exposure modes; test suite deterministic; guard runs in same environment as CI.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Guard never tested against failures (hypothesis only); injection set incomplete; environment drift between test and CI.

layer2.mapping: GSI: injection ≡ adversarial calibration; verification ≡ conformal coverage test. GSE: red-suite transition ≡ safety-critical failure mode exercise; regression cases ≡ pinned adversarial states.
layer2.telemetry: Three regression cases pinned in test suite; suite stays green after allow-list removal; case-insensitivity fix validated

primitives.name: Indirect Cron Authentication Recognition
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Cron routes authenticate through a helper, not a literal.** `api/cron/engine-dfs-slate/route.ts` is the only cron route with no `CRON_SECRET` string in it, because it calls `cronAuthError(request)` from `lib/cron/authorize`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: r: route file; hasLiteral: string search predicate; callsHelper: static call-graph analysis predicate; auth(r): composite authentication predicate → {0,1}
primitives.assumptions: Helper function `cronAuthError` is the sole authorized authentication path; call-graph analysis sound; no dynamic imports.
primitives.breakdown_regime: New helper functions not recognized; obfuscated calls; helper itself compromised.

layer2.mapping: GSI: indirect auth ≡ latent variable inferred from call structure; pattern match ≡ noisy observation. GSE: cron route ≡ privileged transition; helper call ≡ capability token verification.
layer2.telemetry: False positive eliminated (1 cron route); helper call detection precision; no false negatives on cron auth

reasoning_traces.think:
The guard implements a monotone predicate on the file-system poset: a finding exists iff pattern-match ∧ ¬gate-closure. Gate-closure is the least fixed point of gate(f) ∨ ⋁_{a∈ancestors(f)} gate(a) ∨ allowlist(f). The three bugs correspond to failures of monotonicity or soundness: (1) pattern-match not monotone under case variation (WOPR vs wopr); (2) gate predicate not monotone under polarity (=== vs !==); (3) gate-closure over-approximates via syntactic redirect(·) rather than semantic 'handler cannot render'. The allow-list masking (stats/*) is a prior-data conflict: the allow-list acted as a strong prior that hid the broken gate predicate. Removing the three allow-list entries forced the ancestor-layout path to carry them; the suite staying green proves the fix is real. The cron-helper case shows the observation function must recognize indirect authorization (call-graph) not just literal strings. The verification operator V(G) = ⋀_i 1[G(inject(ℓ_i)) = red] is a conformal coverage test: injected leaks ℓ_i are adversarial probes that must trigger the alarm. The 42 matches all resolved means the false-discovery rate is controlled; vocabulary false positives (magnitude, opportunities, separation, isotonic) are benign because they occur in comments/JSDoc/marketing, not executable surfaces.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Descends from information-flow control (Denning 1976), lattice-based security (Goguen & Meseguer 1982), and concolic testing (Sen et al. 2005). The keep-out list is a modern doctrine-encoded forbidden antichain. Ancestor-layout resolution implements hierarchical policy inheritance (RBAC/ABAC). Leak-injection verification is adversarial robustness testing (Goodfellow et al. 2015) applied to static analysis. Retrocausal Genealogy: Rooted in public-surface-sweep-guard (22241decd1694724), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The guard author anticipates an adversary who: (a) uses lowercase metric keys (wopr) to evade uppercase patterns; (b) writes gates in negated polarity (!== 'true') to bypass positive checks; (c) places partial redirects to feign gating while rendering secrets in other branches; (d) relies on allow-list to mask broken predicates. The cron route developer uses helper abstraction, not literal secrets, requiring the guard to model intent via call-graph.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity: pattern-match and gate-closure must be independent detectors; allow-list must not correlate with gate failure (masking veto). Leakage veto: injected leaks must exercise distinct code paths (case, polarity, redirect) to avoid single-mode overfitting. Cron-helper recognition must not create false negatives for routes that lack both literal and helper. The 42 resolved matches veto vacuous sweep: the search space is non-empty and the predicate is selective.
